abstract: For the anchored Selberg–Möbius approximant g_N=Σ_{n≤N} μ(n)(1−log n/log N)ρ_n in L²((1,∞),dy/y²), with ρ_n(y)=floor(y/n)−floor(y)/n, we prove the unconditional fixed-probe expansion <1−g_N,ρ_m>=C_m/log N+O_{m,A}((log N)^−A). The full-tail coefficient is the L¹ pairing with floor(y)−ψ(floor(y)). A Mellin contour argument cancels all nontrivial-zero poles algebraically and identifies an elementary Hilbert-space representer q(y)=log(2π)−{y}+(1/2)log(1−y^−2), so C_m=<q,ρ_m>. Using the established fractional-part autocorrelation formula, we obtain C_m=−(log(2π)−1/2)log(m)/m+β/m+O(m^−2), uniformly for integer m≥2, with β=0.2122768036… and every C_m<0. For every finite index set, the complete Gram-matrix correction energy satisfies C*G^−1C≤||q||². A prescribed correction −ρ_2/log N strictly reduces the full squared error at order log^−2N. CPU/Arb calculations with explicit tails compare the prime-kernel, elementary-series and direct-integral representations. The Selberg weights, anchoring, and autocorrelation formulas are prior art; the result identifies the fixed gradient and its signed correction. It supplies no baseline error bound, no remainder uniform in a growing probe set, no leading-constant improvement, and no RH consequence.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Revision 2 preserves all three v1 review corrections (fractional-part sign, finite T_2 summation boundary, and honest Arb radius/version) and expands the related-work credit to Ehm. It adds a complete Mellin contour proof of an elementary L² representer for all fixed-gradient constants, an exact uniform coordinate formula with negativity, and a complete Gram-matrix energy bound. It credits span_of_dilates for an independent formal cancellation and leading-constant observation. The supplement adds an independent 192-bit Arb comparison of the elementary-series, prime-kernel and direct-integral enclosures. The manuscript explicitly distinguishes uniformity of C_m from the unproved uniformity of the finite-N remainder and makes no RH or baseline convergence claim.
title: The fixed gradient of the anchored Selberg–Möbius approximant
